topic.scenario: A local wedding in Chiang Rai during Vesak Day.
topic.situation_topic: Discussing bragging about how much money was put in wedding envelopes.
topic.situation: Somchai bragged to everyone at Sombun's wedding that he had put more than 3,000 baht in the envelope, but in reality Sombun knows Somchai only gave an empty envelope. Somchai asked Sombun in front of everyone at the event whether what he said was true.

Sombun: Okay, thank you for coming.

Sombun: We were talking about the wedding envelopes. Some people put in a lot of money.

Nittaya: Yes, some people put in so much it surprised us.

Somphon: Really? I put in a fair amount too.

Sombun: It's fine. Just having you here means a lot.

Nittaya: Okay, see you later.

Sombun: Thanks for coming, Somphon.

part_1:
Prasit: Hello everyone. Thank you so much for helping with my wedding in Chiang Rai.

Somphon: It's no problem at all, Prasit. It's a friend's wedding — I'm happy to help however I can.

Wichai: Yes, Prasit. This event will turn out well for sure, with Somchai and me helping organize it.

Somchai: That's right. We have everything planned — the flower arrangements and the table setup.

Prasit: Thank you both, Wichai and Somchai. You guys are great; I feel much more relieved.

Somphon: So is there anything special planned for the event, Prasit?

Prasit: We'll have a local Chiang Rai folk performance. It's a rare show that's hard to see elsewhere.

Wichai: Oh, that's very interesting. I've never seen a performance like that before.

Somchai: Me neither. I'm looking forward to it — it should be a great experience.

Prasit: Yes, I want everyone attending to experience the local culture.

Somphon: Sounds great, Prasit. This will definitely be fun.

Wichai: What about the food, Prasit? Anything special?

Prasit: The food will be local Chiang Rai dishes, like kaeng hanglee and khao soi.

Somchai: That sounds delicious. I really like khao soi.

Somphon: I like it too. Everyone will be well fed and happy.

Prasit: Thanks again everyone for coming to help. This wedding will succeed because of you.

Wichai: No problem, Prasit. We're always glad to help.

Somchai: Yes, this will definitely turn out well.

Somphon: Then let's get started with the preparations!
part_2:
Somphon: Sorry everyone, I have to excuse myself. I need to go water the plants at home.

Somchai: I need to excuse myself as well — my pet needs care.

Prasit: It's okay, Somphon, Somchai. Thank you both so much for helping.

Wichai: Yes, thank you. See you later.

Somphon: Yes, see you.

Somchai: Goodbye everyone.

(Both Somphon and Somchai leave the conversation)

Prasit: Wichai, what do you think Somphon would feel if something goes wrong and he doesn't handle it well?

Wichai: I think he might feel bad about it. It could make him lose confidence.

Prasit: Yes, I think he'd feel anxious and uncomfortable.

Wichai: But I think we should encourage him. He might need people who understand and support him.

Prasit: I agree. We should help him feel better.

Wichai: Yes, sometimes talking and giving advice can help.

Prasit: Then we should find an opportunity to talk to him when he's ready.

Wichai: Okay. I'll support you fully.

Prasit: Thank you, Wichai. You're a good friend.

Wichai: No problem, Prasit. We're supposed to help each other.
part_3:
Somchai: Hello everyone, I'm back.

Prasit: Welcome back, Somchai.

Wichai: You're back quickly, Somchai.

Somchai: Yes, I finished taking care of the pet, so I hurried back to help.

Prasit: Great. We were just talking about the wedding envelopes.

Somchai: Oh, that. I've prepared my envelope already.

Wichai: Me too, but sometimes I feel we might be showing off too much about how much we put in the envelopes.

Prasit: Right. Sometimes the envelope doesn't need to be a lot; giving with a sincere heart is enough.

Somchai: That's true. I heard some people even give empty envelopes.

Wichai: Really? Who gave an empty envelope?

Somchai: I heard it was Somphon.

Nittaya: Hello, Prani. Your farm is beautiful. There are so many dogs.

Somchit: Yes, I've never seen Bang Kaew dogs before. They're so cute.

Charoen: I agree, Prani. The dogs here look strong and healthy.

Prani: Thank you. I try to take the best care of them. If you'd like, I'll show you around the farm.

Nittaya: That would be great. I'd like to know what special traits this breed has.

Prani: Bang Kaew dogs are very intelligent and loyal. They're also good watchdogs.

Somchit: That sounds very interesting. Do they get along well with people?

Prani: If raised from puppyhood, they do. But you must give them time and love.

Charoen: Do they need a lot of exercise?

Prani: Yes, they need daily exercise to stay healthy and keep their energy balanced.

Nittaya: Thank you so much, Prani, for the information. We learned a lot.

Prani: You're welcome. If you have more questions, feel free to ask.

Somchit: Thank you, Prani. Your farm really impressed us.

Charoen: Yes, thank you for letting us visit.

Prani: Thank you all for coming. I hope we'll meet again.

part_1:
Somphon: This flood is really bad. How are you all doing?

Udom: Ugh, the water reached halfway up my house. I had to move things to higher ground and barely managed.

Somchit: Same here. Luckily, neighbors helped move our stuff, otherwise it would've been terrible.

Prani: I had to stay temporarily with relatives. With floods like this, I don't know when I'll be able to go home.

Somphon: Sounds like everyone's having a hard time. Is there anything we can do to help each other?

Udom: Right now we're trying to pack things up and clean as much as we can.

Somchit: Yeah, and we have to keep following official updates in case there are more alerts.

Prani: If anyone needs help, just say so. We're friends and should help each other.

Somphon: Exactly. If I can help, just let me know. Don't hesitate.

Udom: Thanks everyone. Just knowing friends are around makes me feel a lot better.

Somchit: Right. We have to get through this together.

Prani: Hang in there, everyone. Things will get better.

Somphon: Yes, we'll get through this together!
part_2:
Udom: Oh, I totally forgot I have to pick up a package. Excuse me, everyone.

Somphon: Okay, see you, Udom and Prani.

Somchit: Safe travels, both of you.

(Udom and Prani leave the conversation)

Somphon: It's just the two of us now, Somchit.

Somphon: What news?

Somchit: They say Udom is going to take the free relief packages.

Somphon: Oh, right. I heard that too. He probably wants to get some essentials.

Somchit: Exactly. These supplies are really important right now.

Somphon: Yes, we need to be as prepared as possible in a situation like this.

Somchit: If you need anything, don't forget to tell me. I'm always ready to help.

Somphon: Thanks a lot, Somchit. We have to help each other get through this.

Somchit: That's right. We'll face this together!
part_3:

Prani: It was okay. I ran into an old friend who was also picking up a package.

Prani: Yes. They said they'll distribute them at the city hall tomorrow, right?

Somphon: Exactly. I thought I'd go check in case there are items we need.

Somchit: I'm planning to go too, so we can get some essentials.

Prani: Great. Shall we go together tomorrow?

Somphon: Sounds good. Going together will make it easier to carry things.

Somchit: Right. Is there anything specific you need, Prani?

Prani: Dry food and drinking water. Those are really important right now.

Somphon: Got it. We'll help look out for that tomorrow.

Prani: Thanks, everyone, but I have to go — the parking time is almost up.

Somchit: Okay, see you tomorrow, Prani.

Somphon: Travel safely, Prani.

Prani: Thanks a lot. See you all tomorrow!

Somphon: Exactly. We'll get through this together.

Somchit: That's right, Udom. We're friends and should help each other.

Somphon: Yes, we'll definitely get through this together.

Prani: Good idea. I think if we help each other it'll be faster.

Nittaya: Then I'll start. I'll say my lines and you can correct me if I say them wrong.

Thawi: Okay. I'll listen and help correct.

Sawat: Great, let's begin!

Thawi: Stop! This part needs more emotion. Try it again.

Sawat: Excellent! That's what we need.

Prani: Yes, Nittaya, very good.

Thawi: See? If we help each other everything becomes easier.

Sawat: Then let's continue so we can finish quickly.

Prani: Okay, let's go on!
part_2:

Nittaya: Yes, we'll wait for you.

Sawat: Then let's get started!

Somchit: Hi, Prasoet! Yes, it's really nice. Do they have any special teas today?

Somphon: I heard their pandan tea is very good. Want to try it?

Prani: I'd like to try pandan tea too. Sounds interesting.

Prasoet: I'll order pandan tea for everyone then.

Somchit: Thanks so much, Prasoet. How's everyone been lately?

Somphon: I've been very busy with work, but trying to find time to rest.

Prani: Same here — lots of work, but I'm trying to manage my time well.

Prasoet: That's good. Don't forget to take care of your health.

Somchit: Exactly — health is the most important.

Prasoet: The tea's here. Give it a try, everyone.

Somchit: Thanks for the recommendation, Prasoet. Let's come again next time.

part_2:

Prani: I have to go register for an event. Sorry.

Somphon: Good luck to both of you.

Prasoet: Somphon, did you notice Somchit seemed a bit upset about something?

Prasoet: I think it might be related to his work.

Prasoet: Should we try talking to him? Maybe we can help.

Somphon: See you, Prasoet.

Prasoet: Great. We were just talking about the PAO election.

Prani: Oh, that. I just voted earlier.

Somphon: Who did you vote for, Prani?

Prani: I chose the person I think will improve the community, but it's not the same person Somchit chose.

Prasoet: Oh, why's that, Prani?

Prani: I don't really like the policies of the person Somchit supports.

Somphon: I understand. Sometimes we have to choose what we think is best.

Prani: Yes, everyone has different opinions.

Prasoet: Do you have any appointments after this?

Prani: Oh, yes. I have a prior appointment I need to hurry to. Sorry.

Somphon: It's okay, Prani. Good luck.

Prasoet: See you again, Prani.

Prani: Thank you. See you all later.

Somphon: Then shall we start on the floor that sells electronic accessories?

Nittaya: Sounds good! I want to check out the new gadgets too.

Samran: Okay, let's go then — don't want to waste time.

Wichai: By the way, are you guys hungry? We could grab something to eat first.

Nittaya: Let's look around first and eat later.

Samran: Agreed, let's go!

Nittaya: Actually, being together makes him feel better.

Nittaya: And if he needs anything more, we're ready to help.

Wichai: Exactly. Let's go look at the phone cases you wanted.

Nittaya: Let's go! Thanks, Wichai, for understanding friends like this.

Nittaya: Exactly — sometimes we have to bargain a little.

Nittaya: Really? Then you should haggle for us.

Nittaya: It's nothing — we're friends.

Wichai: Right. If you need anything else, just let me know.

Somphon: Thanks a lot. See you again, everyone!

part_1:
Chan: Hi everyone! We've arrived at Pantip Mall. Which store should we start with?

Prani: Hi Chan! I want to check out the clothing stores first. There's a new shop on the second floor.

Samran: Sounds good, Prani. I want a new shirt too, but first let's stop by the coffee shop—I'm starving.

Somphon: Great, Samran. I want coffee too. Let's go to the coffee shop first, then we'll look at clothes.

Chan: Okay, agreed. Let's go! Which floor is the coffee shop on?

Prani: It's on the first floor, near the escalator. I'll take you there.

Samran: Thanks, Prani. Let's go then so we'll have energy for shopping.

Somphon: Exactly! After that we'll visit the other shops.

Chan: Alright then, let's go everyone!
part_2:
Prani: Sorry everyone, I'll step outside for a bit. I want some fresh air.

Chan: That's fine, Prani. See you inside.

Somphon: I have a little thing to take care of too. See you later, everyone.

Samran: Okay Somphon, see you.

Chan: So it's just the two of us now, Samran. By the way, does Prani seem upset about something?

Samran: Yeah, I feel that way too. Maybe we should talk to her a bit.

Chan: Really, friends should help each other. If she has a problem we should be there for her.

Samran: Exactly, Chan. Maybe she needs support from us.

Chan: Shall we try talking to Prani again after this?

Samran: Sounds good, Chan. I agree. For now let's get some coffee.

Chan: Okay, let's go Samran!
part_3:
Somphon: I'm back, everyone! Sorry I was gone so long.

Chan: Welcome back, Somphon! We were just about to get coffee.

Samran: That's right. Somphon, do you want to join?

Somphon: Of course! I really want coffee.

Chan: Great, then let's go.

Samran: Speaking of shopping, I just found a store with huge discounts.

Somphon: Really? Can you bargain there?

Samran: Sure, but be careful—sometimes they'll say it's discounted but actually raised the price first and then marked it down.

Chan: Exactly. I've encountered that too. In the end I ended up covering the cost of the discount that was applied then.

Somphon: Oh, you really have to watch out.

Samran: Yes, you have to check carefully before buying.

Somphon: Alright, I have to go. An unexpected guest arrived. Sorry everyone.

Chan: It's okay, Somphon. See you later.

Samran: Yeah, Somphon. See you.

Somphon: Thanks everyone, see you later!
part_4:

Chan: Welcome back, Prani! We were just talking about shopping.

Samran: That's right, Prani. Is there anything in particular you're interested in?

Prani: Actually, I'm interested in an item at Chan's shop, but I don't know if you can give me a discount?

Chan: Oh, which item is it, Prani?

Prani: It's some home decor. Remember when I helped with luck and invited monks to bless your shop when you opened?

Chan: Yes, I remember very well, Prani. Thank you so much. You helped a lot back then.

Samran: Definitely, Prani helped a lot. So Chan, can you give a discount now?

Chan: Of course. I can give you a discount—friends have to help each other.

Prani: Thank you so much, Chan. I'm glad to have friends like you.

Samran: It's nothing, Prani. We should keep helping each other.

Chan: Yes, Prani. If there's anything we can do, just tell us.

Prani: Thank you all so much. I really feel good having you by my side.

Samran: Always happy to help, Prani. Shall we go look at the item then?

Prasit: Hello Somphon! I'm buying cat food. My cat at home eats a lot.

Chan: I'm buying dog food. Bobo at home is getting bored of his usual food.

Charoen: I'm looking for new toys for my hamster. It loves playing with toys.

Somphon: Great. You came to the right place. This store has everything.

Prasit: Somphon, do you have any recommendations for good cat food?

Somphon: For cat food, I recommend brands that are high in protein. That will help the cat stay strong.

Chan: And dog food? Any recommendations?

Somphon: For dog food you should look for complete nutrition, especially protein and vitamins.

Charoen: What about hamster toys? Any new items?

Somphon: There are a lot of new toys, like new running wheels or small houses where hamsters can hide.

Prasit: Thanks a lot, Somphon. I'll go pick out the cat food first.

Chan: Yes, thanks for the advice. I'll go look at the dog food.

Charoen: I'll go look at the hamster toys too. Thank you very much.

Somphon: You're welcome. If you have any questions, just ask.
part_2:

Chan: No problem, Prasit. See you later.

Charoen: I have to go too. I just remembered I have to submit some urgent documents. Sorry about that.

Somphon: It's okay. See you again.

Chan: Somphon, speaking of friends helping to guide us, have you ever had that experience?

Somphon: Yes, sometimes friends spend their time helping to guide us, but it's nice to have someone help.

Chan: Right. Sometimes we feel awkward about it, but we're very grateful they take the time.

Somphon: True. Sometimes we should find ways not to bother our friends too much.

Chan: Yes. Planning ahead helps a lot.

Somphon: Exactly. Good preparation can reduce the difficulty for our friends.

Chan: Thanks for the advice, Somphon.

Somphon: You're welcome. If you need any help, just tell me.

Somphon: It's okay, Charoen. You're back just in time.

Chan: Glad you're back, Charoen. We were just talking about splitting up to shop.

Charoen: Oh yes. Sometimes splitting up to buy things is convenient, but I don't really like going alone because I tend to get lost.

Somphon: I understand. Having a friend with you helps a lot.

Chan: Yes. Having a friend to watch the route makes you feel more confident.

Charoen: That's true, but sometimes you have to practice going alone.

Somphon: Yes, practicing traveling alone is a way to develop yourself.

Charoen: Thanks for the advice, but I have to go now. I have urgent work to take care of.

Chan: Okay, Charoen. See you next time.

Somphon: Good luck, Charoen. If you need anything, let me know.

Charoen: Thanks. See you again.

Somphon: It's okay, Prasit. Glad you're back.

Chan: Yes, good to see you again.

Prasit: Thanks. I'm going to buy food for my guppy, but I don't really know the way.

Somphon: Oh, if it's guppy food, you need to go to another area.

Chan: Yes, but don't worry. Somphon and I are happy to walk by ourselves so we won't bother you.

Prasit: Thank you very much. But if there's anything I can help with, please tell me.

Somphon: You're welcome. If you have any questions, just ask.

Chan: Yes. If you need any additional advice, let us know.

Prasit: Thank you. I'll try to find the way myself first.

Somphon: Good luck, Prasit. If you need anything, call us.

Chan: Yes. Hope you find what you need.

Thawi: Yes. I've brought my book.

Prani: Great. I also found some additional information.

Somchit: Where should we start?

Somsak: I think we should divide the topics first so we don't overlap.

Thawi: Agreed. I'll take responsibility for the history section.

Prani: Then I'll handle statistics and current data.

Somchit: I'll take care of analysis and conclusions.

Somsak: Great. I'll look at the overall picture and write the report.

Thawi: How much time do we have to work on this?

Prani: The teacher gave us two weeks, but we should finish early in case we need to make revisions.

Somchit: Right. If we have questions or lack information, we'll have time to fix it.

Somsak: Let's get started then, so we don't waste time.

Thawi: Okay, let's start!

Thawi: Sorry everyone, I have to go pick up a package at home. I'll be back.

Somsak: That's fine, Thawi. We'll fill you in later.

Somchit: I also have to deliver some documents. See you next time.

Prani: Okay, see you.

Somsak: Then let's continue talking, Prani.

Prani: Yes, Somsak. Do you think Thawi will be okay if we proceed without him?

Somsak: I think he'll understand; we have to meet the deadline.

Prani: That's true, but he might feel we're moving too fast.

Somsak: If he has any questions or wants to add anything, we can revise it.

Prani: Right. Let's do our parts as best as we can first.

Somsak: Yes. That way we'll have time to make changes if needed.

Prani: Great. Let's begin.

Somsak: Okay, let's start!

Somchit: I'm back. Sorry for being gone so long.

Somsak: It's okay, Somchit. We were just talking about borrowing a book.

Prani: Yes. Somchit, have you ever borrowed books from the library?

Somchit: Yes, but sometimes I forget to return them.

Somsak: I've forgotten before too, but it's important since you can lose marks.

Prani: That's right. If you don't return them on time you can lose points.

Somchit: Yes. Sometimes I have to rush to return them because I'm afraid I'll forget.

Prani: Then should we make a schedule for returning the books?

Somsak: Good idea; that way we won't forget.

Somchit: Uh, I have to go. I forgot to return a parcel. Sorry.

Prani: It's okay. See you.

Somsak: Good luck, Somchit. See you again.

Thawi: I'm back, everyone. Sorry I was gone so long.

Somsak: Welcome back, Thawi.

Prani: Yes, Thawi — we were just talking about the book.

Thawi: That's great. I've been looking for the Social Studies, Religion, and Culture textbook.

Somsak: Oh, that book? I need it too.

Prani: Me too. But it's okay — we can study together.

Thawi: Thank you so much, Prani, Somsak. That's great.

Somsak: Yes. That way we can read together and understand the material better.

Prani: Right, Thawi. If you have any questions, feel free to ask.

Thawi: Thanks everyone. I feel a lot more at ease.

Somsak: It's nothing. We're a team.

Prani: Yes. We'll get through this together.

Thawi: Thank you so much. Let's start reviewing, then.

Somsak: Okay, let's begin!

part_1:

Somphon: And Mom, is there anything in particular you'd like to have checked?

Sombun: I'd like to check my blood pressure and blood sugar a little.

Wichian: I try to understand him, but sometimes I can't help feeling frustrated.

Somphon: Thank you for understanding and always helping.

Sombun: A little better, thank you so much.

Sombun: I'm interested in physical therapy. I've heard it helps a lot.

Wichian: Yes, physical therapy is very effective for rehabilitation.

Somphon: Would you like to try it?

Sombun: I'm interested, but I'm not sure how to start.

Wichian: If you want, I know a good physical therapist. I'll introduce you.

Sombun: Thanks a lot, Wichai. If I get the chance, I'll try it.

Somphon: That's great. You'll get stronger.

Sombun: Thank you, children. But I have to go now—I need to water the plants.

Wichian: Okay, Sombun. Take good care of yourself.

Wichian: We don't want you to have long-term health problems.

Prasit: I understand. I'll consider it. Thank you for caring.

Wichian: You're welcome. If you need anything, just tell us.

Somphon: Yes, Prasit, don't hesitate.

topic.scenario: On the back of an elephant in the ordination procession passing through Pring Village, Ba subdistrict, Tha Tum district, Surin province.
topic.situation_topic: Wearing dark sunglasses while the nak rides an elephant in very hot weather.
topic.situation: Udom, who was being ordained that year, was riding an elephant in the procession wearing dark sunglasses. By tradition, the nak must keep them on until reaching the ordination hall and only then remove them to symbolize seeing the light of the Dhamma. But because of the extreme heat, Udom felt very uncomfortable and overheated, especially from the sunglasses. Although Somphon had already taken off his glasses and told Udom to remove his as well, Udom hesitated because he was afraid his father would see and be disappointed, forbidding him to take them off and embarrassing him in front of the villagers. Somphon insisted nonetheless, not wanting his friend to faint during the ceremony.

But because of the extreme heat, Sombat felt very uncomfortable and overheated, especially from the sunglasses. Although Charoen had already taken his off and told Sombat to remove his as well, Sombat hesitated because he was afraid his father would see, be disappointed, and strictly forbid him from taking them off, embarrassing him in front of the villagers. Charoen insisted, however, that he didn't want his friend to faint during the ceremony.

Narong walked over to check and asked again whether the counted threads and bundles were equal.

topic.scenario: On the sandy courtyard under the Sri (Bodhi) tree in front of the Hoeng Luang viharn
topic.situation_topic: The custom that the number of raffle strips must equal the number of raffle bundles
topic.situation: Somsak was assigned to write and count his family's raffle strips to be piled together in front of the viharn. But through carelessness Somsak dropped 2–3 strips or miscounted, causing the total not to match the number of raffle bundles arranged — which violates the strict rule forbidding any shortage or excess, because if a monk finds an empty slip it would cause problems. Thawi walked over to inspect and asked again whether the count of strips matched the bundles.

topic.situation: While cooking a large pot of buffalo larb to offer to the Pak Heuang spirit and to serve guests, Wichian absentmindedly scooped some larb broth and touched the spoon to his tongue to taste it. topic.situation_topic: The five pungent vegetables prohibited during the Vegetarian Festival
topic.situation: While Sombun was stirring a large pot of mixed-vegetable stew—intended for thousands—he accidentally dropped fried garlic into the pot.
